questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

By the time I turn thirty / I would had visited every / continent in the world and have gained / a wealth of knowledge and experience.

options.text: By the time I turn thirty
a wealth of knowledge and experience
continent in the world and have gained

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the third part of the given sentence, the verb phrase 'would had' is incorrect.
 
• The correct form should be 'would have' instead of 'would had'.
 
• The correct sentence should be: ***I would have visited every***.

Hence, the correct sentence is** "By the time I turn thirty I would have visited__ every continent in the world and have gained a wealth of knowledge and experience."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When using **modal verbs** like **would, could, should, etc.**, they are always followed by the **base form of the verb 'have'**.
 
• Example: ***She would have gone** to the party if she had known about it.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) It is a / (B) state of chaos / (C) since the / (D) chairman resigned.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'A' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the first part of the given sentence, the error lies in the tense used.
 
• Given that the situation is ongoing since the chairman resigned, the **present perfect continuous tense** should be used instead of the present simple.
 
• The correct form should be "It **has been** a state of chaos since the chairman resigned."

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *It **has been** a state of chaos since the chairman resigned*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If an action started in the past and continues to the present, the present perfect or present perfect continuous tense is used.
 
 
• **Example:** *She has been working here for five years.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Her dedication to her work was _______ what anyone had expected.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct preposition to use in this context is **'beyond'**, which means** 'at or to the further side of**' or** 'more than'.**
 
• The sentence implies that **her dedication exceeded the expectations, and 'beyond' appropriately conveys this meaning.**
 
• The correct preposition here is **'beyond.'**

Hence, the correct statement is** '*Her dedication to her work was beyond__ what anyone had expected*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 'over'** implies **movement, direction, or position **but** does not** fit the context of exceeding expectations.
 
• **Option 3 'beside' **means **next to,** which is spatial and **not suitable** for this context.
 
• **Option 4 'through' **suggests** moving in one side and out the other**, which **does not convey** the intended meaning of exceeding.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• In the first part of the given sentence, the comparative form 'junior than' is incorrect.
 
• The correct usage should be 'junior to' instead of 'junior than'.
 
• In English, words like junior, senior, superior, inferior, prefer etc., are followed by 'to' rather than 'than'.
 
• Therefore, the correct form should be 'junior to'.

Hence, the correct statement is '***Tushar is junior to__ all his colleagues*.'**

• **Example:** *She is **senior to** me in the company*.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) One of / (B) my brothers write / (C) novels for / (D) leisure.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the singular form of the verb 'write' is incorrect.
 
• In the given sentence, the **subject 'one of my brothers'** is **singular** and requires a **singular verb**.
 
• Therefore, the correct form of the verb should be 'writes' instead of 'write'.

Hence, the correct statement is: ***One of my brothers writes__ novels for leisure*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• **Example:** ***One of the students is__ absent today*.**

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Henry is known / as an excellent writer / and good communicator / in English.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase 'and good communicator' is incorrect.
 
• It should be 'and a good communicator' to maintain the **parallel structure of the sentence.**
 
• Parallel structure means using the same pattern of words to show that two or more ideas have the same level of importance.
 
• In this case, since '**an excellent writer' **is preceded by an article **'an'**, '**a good communicator**' should also be preceded by an article** 'a' **to keep the sentence structure consistent.

Hence, the correct statement is **'*Henry is known as an excellent writer__ and__ a good communicator__ in English*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Parallel structure is important in writing because it improves **coherence and consistency.**
 
• It helps in making sentences clearer and easier to read.
 
• When items in a series or list follow the same grammatical structure, it ensures that the sentence is balanced and flows smoothly.
 
 
• **Example:** *She likes** reading, writing, and jogging.***
